summary: The SI Scholarship for Global Professionals is awarded by the Swedish Institute, a Swedish government agency, for full-time one- or two-year English-taught master's studies at Swedish universities. It is for citizens of 34 listed countries who have work experience and leadership experience, and who are admitted to an eligible programme in Governance, Public Health, Entrepreneurship and Innovation, or STEM. The scholarship pays the tuition fee, a monthly allowance and a one-time travel grant, and gives membership of the SI Network for Global Professionals. It does not include insurance.
eligibility_notes:
Applicants must be citizens of one of the 34 eligible countries; they do not need to live in that country when applying. Dual citizens of two eligible countries must pick one citizenship; applying twice with different citizenships disqualifies both applications. Dual citizens whose other citizenship is a country not on the latest OECD DAC list of ODA recipients are not eligible. Public sector employees in Georgia and Belarus are not eligible.

The applicant must be liable to pay tuition fees in Sweden (the scholarship then pays them), must have applied through the central admissions service University Admissions (paying its application fee on time) to an eligible English-taught master's programme, and must be admitted or conditionally admitted to that programme on the first admissions day, 1 April 2027. Programmes where the applicant is only a reserve are not considered and there are no scholarships for late admissions. Changing the admissions result (for example declining an offer) takes the application out of the running. SI sets no English-language or GPA requirement of its own; the universities and University Admissions assess these.

Work experience is required (employment full-time or part-time, freelancing or entrepreneurship; internships do not count), but the applicant need not be employed at the time of applying. Experience in line with the chosen field is prioritised. Applicants from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine need proof of work experience with no hour requirement, but more experience is prioritised. Applicants from the other 28 countries need at least 3,000 hours of work experience before February 2027, from at most three employers. Leadership experience is also required, shown through work, entrepreneurship or civil society involvement, with no minimum hours; strong leadership experience from employment is prioritised. Current employees should talk to their employer about leave: that is their own responsibility.

Not eligible: people currently enrolled in or holding a degree from a Swedish university or university college; people who have lived in Sweden for two years or more in total before the scholarship period starting August 2027; previous SI scholarship holders for studies in Sweden; Swedish or EU/EEA citizens, holders of a Swedish permanent residence permit, or holders of a temporary work or family-based residence permit linked to a Swedish/EU/EEA citizen; and dual citizens of a country not on the DAC list. Exceptions: Ukrainians living in Sweden under the Temporary Protection Directive may apply, and Moldovans who also hold Romanian citizenship may apply but must state the eligible citizenship. People already enrolled in a master's in Sweden cannot apply for their second year.

Applicants should show how their studies will support sustainable development in their home country and region.
age_experience_notes: No age limit is stated. Work experience: 3,000 hours before February 2027 from up to three employers for applicants from most countries; proof of any work experience (no hour minimum) for Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine. Leadership experience has no minimum hours. Example in the FAQ: 40 hours a week for 50 weeks for one year plus 12 hours a week for 28 weeks for three years gives 3,008 hours, which meets the rule.
funding_summary: For the whole master's study period SI pays the tuition fee directly to the Swedish university each semester, pays a monthly allowance of SEK 12,000 for living costs, and pays a one-time travel grant of SEK 15,000 (SEK 10,000 for scholars from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine; not for students already living in Sweden). Scholars also get membership of the SI Network for Global Professionals and later the Sweden Alumni Network. Insurance, grants for family members and the University Admissions application fee are not included. The scholarship covers only the awarded programme and period: no change of programme and no extension.
programmes_note: English-taught master's programmes in four study fields: Governance, Public Health, Entrepreneurship and Innovation, and STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics). Only programmes on SI's eligible list qualify. The list for 2027/2028 was due to be published on the SI call page on 13 November 2026 and was not yet on the page when it was read. Bachelor's, PhD and postdoctoral studies, single courses and exchanges are not covered.
institutions_note: Eligible programmes are at Swedish universities and university colleges, mostly applied to through University Admissions (up to four programmes). Stockholm School of Economics and Konstfack - University of Arts, Crafts and Design run separate intakes; their applicants get no University Admissions number and SI receives a separate admitted-students list from the Stockholm School of Economics. A scholarship application may list up to four eligible programmes, and a programme at the Stockholm School of Economics or Konstfack may be added as a fifth.

summary.detail: Full-time, one- or two-year English-taught master's studies at Swedish universities in Governance, Public Health, Entrepreneurship and Innovation, or STEM, starting in the autumn semester (August) 2027. Applicant must be admitted to an eligible programme on 1 April 2027 and be liable for tuition fees. SI sets no language or GPA minimum; the universities do. The scholarship cannot be moved to another programme and the period cannot be extended or changed.
summary.source_text: full-time, one- or two-year master's studies

benefits.limit_text: Full tuition fee, paid directly by SI to the Swedish university each semester
benefits.conditions: Applicant must be liable to pay tuition fees when applying. The University Admissions application fee is not covered.

benefits.limit_text: SEK 12,000 per month throughout the study period
benefits.conditions: For living expenses. No extension or change to the awarded scholarship period.

benefits.limit_text: One-time travel grant of SEK 15,000; SEK 10,000 for scholars from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine
benefits.conditions: Single payment; does not apply to students already living in Sweden.
SI advises checking with the university about insurance for international students.

benefits.limit_text: No separate housing payment is named by the source
benefits.conditions: The monthly allowance is described as covering living expenses; accommodation is not mentioned as a separate benefit.

benefits.limit_text: Grants for family members are not provided
benefits.conditions: The University Admissions application fee is also not covered.

benefits.limit_text: Membership of the SI Network for Global Professionals during the studies, and of the Sweden Alumni Network afterwards
benefits.conditions: Platform for career development and networking.

requirements.text: Application to an eligible master's programme through University Admissions by 15 January 2027, with the personal application number (seven or eight digits) copied correctly into the SI application; a wrong number disqualifies the application. Applicants only to the Stockholm School of Economics or Konstfack enter eight zeroes.
Curriculum vitae on SI's CV template for 2027/2028, at most three pages; other formats, including Europass, are disqualified and extra pages are ignored

Proof of work and leadership experience on SI's template for 2027/2028: up to three work experience forms and up to two leadership forms, each at most one page, merged into one PDF of at most five pages (work forms first, then leadership forms, each in reverse date order). Each form is typed, printed, signed by a referee who knows the work in a professional capacity, stamped with an official stamp of the organisation or a notary office, and uploaded as one PDF.

Two letters of reference from two different referees on SI's template, typed, printed, signed and stamped, scanned and uploaded as one PDF. One must be based on work experience; the second may be based on work or on engagements outside work (a merit if based on entrepreneurship or civil society or network involvement). Translations must be done by a notarised translator and uploaded with the original in one PDF.
Photocopy of a valid passport or national ID card clearly showing name, citizenship and photograph
Motivation for applying, written in the application portal; some applicants may be randomly asked to record a short video presentation
The whole application must be in English, on the current year's SI templates; documents not requested by SI are not considered

application_steps.title: Apply to master's programmes through University Admissions
application_steps.detail: Between 16 October 2026 and 15 January 2027, apply for up to four eligible English-taught master's programmes in the University Admissions portal and pay its application fee on time (SI charges no fee). Save the personal application number you receive. Stockholm School of Economics and Konstfack applicants use their own separate processes. Missing the University Admissions deadline or steps makes you ineligible.

application_steps.title: Prepare the SI documents from the templates published 13 November
application_steps.detail: SI publishes the eligible programme list and the document templates on its call page on 13 November 2026. Prepare the CV, proof of work and leadership experience, two letters of reference and passport or ID copy exactly on the templates; only that year's templates are valid. Referees should be reachable until the results on 22 April 2027.

application_steps.title: Submit one online scholarship application, 8 to 24 February 2027
application_steps.detail: Apply in SI's online application portal, which is open for two weeks and closes at 14:59 CET on 24 February 2027. Submit only one application however many programmes you applied for, listing up to four eligible programmes (a fifth at the Stockholm School of Economics or Konstfack is possible), write the motivation in English, and upload each required document once. No late applications are accepted.

application_steps.title: SI screens applications for eligibility, 25 February to 31 March
application_steps.detail: SI disqualifies applications that do not meet the eligibility criteria or that have an incomplete application, the wrong forms, a missing valid stamp or other instruction failures. Eligible applications are then scored with attention to the purpose of the programme: SI looks for talented professionals with capability, an existing platform and the ambition to contribute to their home country and region.

application_steps.title: Admission results on 1 April 2027 decide who stays in the running
application_steps.detail: University Admissions passes the admission results directly to SI on 1 April 2027. You stay in the running only if you are admitted or conditionally admitted to an eligible programme that day and make no change to the admission result. Reserves and waiting-list applicants are not considered.

application_steps.title: Final evaluation and announcement on 22 April 2027
application_steps.detail: SI makes a final evaluation of the remaining eligible applications. It aims for equal gender balance and for as many eligible countries as possible, within its budget, but has no quotas by country, field or university. Recipients are announced on the SI website on 22 April 2027; only those offered a scholarship are notified.

application_steps.title: Accept or decline the scholarship offer
application_steps.detail: Each recipient gets an official offer by email by the end of April 2027 and must accept or decline within the deadline stated in the offer. The email address given in the application must be correct.

application_steps.title: Study the awarded programme and join the networks
application_steps.detail: The scholarship supports only the awarded master's programme and period; changes of programme and extensions are not allowed, and deferral is only possible after studies have started. SI pays tuition to the university each semester. Scholars join the SI Network for Global Professionals and afterwards the Sweden Alumni Network. Insurance must be arranged through the university or the scholar.
